info.title: HuntDeck API
info.description: Everything HuntDeck shows, as JSON or plain text. There is no login and no token: HuntDeck is reached only from your own machine or private network. Lists come a page at a time (limit and offset) with the total; errors are JSON with a sentence in error.

tags.name: Hunt board
tags.description: The hunt board's summary: what HuntDeck holds, this week's news, and the best programs to hunt now.

tags.name: Programs
tags.description: Programs, one program in full, and its scope for Burp Suite or ZAP.

tags.name: Targets
tags.description: Scope targets across every program, ready to pipe into recon tools.

tags.name: Scope check
tags.description: Which programs a host, IP or URL, or a list of them, is in or out of scope for.

tags.name: Activity
tags.description: What changed on the platforms, and disclosed reports.

tags.name: Stats
tags.description: The Stats pages' numbers: every platform and all of them together, a platform's programs, and programs' public numbers.

tags.name: HuntDeck
tags.description: HuntDeck itself: what it holds, polling, and health.

tags.name: Tokens
tags.description: Keys for scripts, minted here and revoked here. A token is another key to the same access gate as the password: it carries no identity, and there are no scopes or roles.

tags.name: Your reports
tags.description: Your own reports on the platforms, as the Reports and Analytics pages show them: titles, states, severities, times and earnings, never write-ups or comments.

get.description: The hunt board's headline numbers (programs, private, open, paying, in-scope entries, wildcards, domains; changes in 24 hours and 7 days), this week's counts (scope added and to how many programs, wildcards and domains among it, new programs and invites, bounty changes), programs that reopened, paused or keep flipping this week, and the top hunts: the highest HuntScores you can hunt now. The board's fresh targets are /api/v1/targets?sort=best, its changes /api/v1/changes.

Programs with the Programs page's filters and sorts, with their HuntScore, bounty range, scope counts and requirements. Sorted by name unless sort says otherwise. Each has numbers: the Programs page's columns (paid and received in 90 days, total paid, average bounty, resolved in 90 days, response times), estimates flagged. Answers carry an ETag and a Last-Modified: send either back (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since) to get 304 Not Modified, with no body, while the answer is unchanged.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Only these platforms' programs: one, or several separated by commas, as hackerone,bugcrowd (hackerone, bugcrowd, intigriti, yeswehack; independent: programs added by hand).

parameters.name: not
parameters.description: Leave out programs whose name or handle contains any of these words, separated by spaces or commas. A word starting with - in q does the same.

parameters.name: watch
parameters.description: Only these programs, as platform/handle separated by commas (at most 200): the watchlist a browser keeps.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Programs by status: open (the default), paused or closed, all, or no longer listed.

parameters.name: bounty
parameters.description: 1: paying programs only; vdp: programs that don't pay.

parameters.name: top
parameters.description: Top bounty at least this much, in the program's currency: any amount up to 10000000 (the page's chips are 1000, 5000 and 20000).

parameters.name: visibility
parameters.description: Private (invited) or public programs.

parameters.name: invite
parameters.description: Invitations: pending (not accepted yet; platforms that list them: Intigriti) or joined (accepted).

parameters.name: new
parameters.description: Added in-scope assets within.

parameters.name: launched
parameters.description: Launched within.

parameters.name: resumed
parameters.description: Back open after a pause within.

parameters.name: wild
parameters.description: 1: with wildcards in scope.

parameters.name: apps
parameters.description: 1: with Android or iOS apps in scope.

parameters.name: api
parameters.description: 1: with APIs in scope.

parameters.name: creds
parameters.description: 1: offering test credentials.

parameters.name: noreq
parameters.description: 1: known to need nothing beyond an account.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only programs with this tag.

parameters.name: ignored
parameters.description: Ignored programs are left out unless include (with the rest) or only.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name or handle contains; a word starting with - leaves out programs containing it (acme -staging).

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order, as the Programs page's columns: biggest first (rev=1 turns it around); missing values stay last and ties go by name, A to Z, either way; money (paid90, paidall, avgbounty, bounty) sorts within each currency, the most common first; invited puts pending invitations first, then the latest invited or joined.

parameters.name: rev
parameters.description: 1: turn the order around.

parameters.name: trends
parameters.description: 1: add each program's 90-day lines (received, paid, resolved), a point a day, as the Programs page draws them.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only programs whose updated_at is after this: an RFC 3339 time, or a duration back from now (24h, 7d). A program's updated_at moves when HuntDeck first sees it, records a change to it (as Changes lists: scope, policy, status, bounty table…), sees one of its numbers change, or marks it removed (state=removed lists those).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to return, at most 1,000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to skip, for the next page.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: csv hands back the list as the page's spreadsheet export does: every matching program, the same columns, instead of a page of JSON.

get.summary: List programs, each number with its freshness
get.description: Programs with the Programs page's filters and sorts, with their HuntScore, bounty range, scope counts and requirements. Sorted by name unless sort says otherwise. Each has numbers: the Programs page's columns (paid and received in 90 days, total paid, average bounty, resolved in 90 days, response times), estimates flagged. Unlike v1, each value that can be estimated or that polls refresh (bounty, in_scope_entries, out_of_scope_entries, wildcards, domains, apps, apis and each of numbers) is an object: value (as v1 has it), estimated (true where HuntDeck works it out rather than the platform publishing it as it is), source (the platform that publishes it, manual for programs added by hand, or derived: counted or worked out by HuntDeck from what the platform publishes) and updated_at (when the value last changed, to the poll that saw it change: re-read unchanged, it keeps its time; null where it can't be dated). The Methodology page says which numbers each platform publishes and which are estimates. v1 keeps the flat shape. Answers carry an ETag and a Last-Modified: send either back (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since) to get 304 Not Modified, with no body, while the answer is unchanged.

post.description: Accepts the invitation to a private program on its platform (HackerOne with its website login, Bugcrowd or Intigriti), signing in first if it has to, then refreshes that program in the background: its listing, scope and stats. Answers once the platform has accepted, or with 202 if it's slow to (it carries on).

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: The platform.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The program's handle on it, as /api/v1/invites gives it.

202.description: Still accepting: the platform is slow to answer.

404.description: No pending invitation to that program, or the platform's invitations can't be accepted from HuntDeck.

409.description: The platform is turned off in Settings.

get.description: One program in full, as its page has it: bounty range and HuntScore, scope entries and their targets, public stats (times to respond, triage, bounty and resolve, numbers by severity, the bounty table), requirements, test credentials and rules for test traffic, what the platform says about how it runs, its brief (policy, introduction, reward notes, scope and severity notes, FAQ, exclusions), announcements, and its disclosed, resolved and accepted reports. Its changes are /api/v1/changes?program=platform/handle. Answers carry an ETag and a Last-Modified: send either back (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since) to get 304 Not Modified, with no body, while the answer is unchanged.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: The platform. independent: programs added by hand.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The program's handle on it.

parameters.name: parts
parameters.description: Comma separated projection: scope, disclosed, facts, brief, announcements, rules, numbers. Default: everything. An unknown part is a 400.

parameters.name: scope_limit
parameters.description: With parts=scope: entries per answer (default 500).

parameters.name: scope_offset
parameters.description: With parts=scope: entries to skip; scope_total in the answer says how many exist.

get.summary: Get a program, each number with its freshness

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The program's handle on it.

get.description: The program's live scope as Burp Suite advanced scope rules (in-scope targets included, out-of-scope ones excluded): load it under Settings › Project › Scope. Wildcards cover subdomains only. The X-HuntDeck-Generated-At header says when it was made (JSON has no comments to carry it).

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: The platform. independent: programs added by hand.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The program's handle on it.

200.description: A Burp Suite project options file.

get.description: The same scope as a ZAP context (File › Import Context). ZAP's regexes can't express IP ranges, so CIDRs are only in a comment.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: The platform. independent: programs added by hand.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The program's handle on it.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: 1: add <!-- generated_at=<RFC 3339 time> --> after the XML declaration. The X-HuntDeck-Generated-At header has the time either way.

get.description: The program's live scope as a Caido configuration file (docs.caido.io/app/guides/config) holding one scope preset: in-scope hosts in its allowlist, out-of-scope ones in its denylist, as Caido's host globs (*.example.com covers subdomains only). Caido's scope has no paths, so a URL in scope allows its host; out-of-scope paths, IP ranges other than /8, /16, /24 and /32, IPv6 and assets that aren't hosts (apps, hardware) are left out, and X-HuntDeck-Skipped says how many. Start Caido with caido-cli --config on it, or pass config.project.scopes[0] to the SDK's createScope. The X-HuntDeck-Generated-At header says when it was made (JSON has no comments to carry it).

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: The platform. independent: programs added by hand.

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: The program's handle on it.

200.description: A Caido configuration file, named huntdeck-<platform>-<handle>-caido.json.

X-HuntDeck-Skipped.description: How many entries and targets the file leaves out.

get.description: Every in-scope target of a kind across live programs, one per line, deduplicated and streamed, ready to pipe; or with format=json, a page of them with their programs. Paused and ignored programs are left out unless asked for.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: What to list: roots are the registrable domains in scope; all is every kind of address but roots. Assets that aren't addresses list their scope entries: apps (Android and iOS), android, ios, windows, executable, source_code, hardware, smart_contract, ai_model or other.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: In or out of scope.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Only this platform's programs. independent: programs added by hand.

parameters.name: bounty
parameters.description: 1: bounty-eligible targets only.

parameters.name: private
parameters.description: 1: private programs' only.

parameters.name: added
parameters.description: Added within (7d, 30d, 90d, 365d, or any number of days), or since a date (2026-10-01).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only programs with this tag.

parameters.name: include_paused
parameters.description: 1: paused programs' targets too.

parameters.name: include_ignored
parameters.description: 1: ignored programs' targets too.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Target contains.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: best: new targets scored, best first (JSON adds score and reasons).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Plain text, one per line, or JSON.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: 1: as a file download (plain text).

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only targets whose scope entry HuntDeck saw added or edited after this: an RFC 3339 time, or a duration back from now (24h, 7d). Removed scope isn't a target: /api/v1/changes?kind=scope_removed lists removals.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: 1: start the plain-text list with a comment line, # generated_at=<RFC 3339 time> (grep -v '^#' drops it); the lines after it are as without it. Every export also has the time in its X-HuntDeck-Generated-At header.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: JSON: how many to return, at most 5,000 (default 1,000). Plain text: every one unless given; a read-only copy (a public demo) gives at most 5,000 lines at a time, with a Link header to the next ones.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to skip.

200.description: Targets, one per line (or JSON with format=json).

Link.description: Read-only copy, plain text: where the next lines are, when there are more (rel="next").

X-Targets-Limit.description: Read-only copy, plain text: the most lines this answer gives.

get.description: Which programs a host, IP or URL is in or out of scope for (the most specific rule wins; a wildcard covers subdomains, not the domain itself), removed scope that used to cover it, live scope under it, and, when nothing else matches, scope that mentions it. Answers carry an ETag and a Last-Modified: send either back (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since) to get 304 Not Modified, with no body, while the answer is unchanged.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: A host, IP or URL, or part of a host name.

post.description: A list of hosts, IPs or URLs in the body, one per line (blank lines, # comments and repeats skipped; at most 20,000 lines, 4 MB; 2,000 lines on a read-only demo). Each gets a verdict: in (in scope for some program), out (only excluded) or none. format=txt returns just the in-scope lines, to filter recon output.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: JSON verdicts, or just the in-scope lines.

parameters.name: comment
parameters.description: With format=txt, 1: start the list with a comment line, # generated_at=<RFC 3339 time> (grep -v '^#' drops it); the lines after it are as without it. The X-HuntDeck-Generated-At header has the time either way.

requestBody.description: One host, IP or URL per line.

200.description: Verdicts (or the in-scope lines with format=txt).

get.description: What changed on the platforms: programs added, removed, paused and reopened, scope added, removed and edited, bounty and policy changes, announcements. Every change, oldest first unless order=newest.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: From when: an RFC 3339 time or how long ago (24h, 7d).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only these kinds, comma-separated.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Only this platform's programs. independent: programs added by hand.

parameters.name: bounty
parameters.description: 1: changes to paying programs only; vdp: to programs that don't pay.

parameters.name: program
parameters.description: Only this program's changes, as platform/handle: what its Changes tab shows.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: newest: newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to return, at most 1,000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to skip, for the next page.

400.description: since isn't a time or duration.

get.description: Disclosed reports across programs (HackerOne Hacktivity), with the Disclosed page's filters, newest first.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Title contains.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Only this platform's programs.

parameters.name: severity
parameters.description: Severity; high+ is critical or high, none unrated.

parameters.name: weakness
parameters.description: Only this weakness (CWE name).

parameters.name: paid
parameters.description: 1: with a public bounty.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Disclosed within (7d, 30d, 90d, 365d) or since a date.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to return, at most 1,000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to skip, for the next page.

get.description: The Stats page: every platform, and all of them together. Each has its open, paying and free programs, assets and wildcards in scope, scope added and removed in 30 days, reports received and paid in 90 days (as the Programs list sums them) and a year of months (open, paying, assets and wildcards at each month's end; scope added, programs that added scope, launched, disclosed, valid reports, bounties shown and median days to resolve), with the points of the 90-day lines by day. Null is a number the platform doesn't publish.

get.description: This API as OpenAPI 3.1, for Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, client generators or AI tools; its server is the address you asked from.
ok while the database answers, for container health checks; it never says why not.

Targets ranked by whether you can start today and what the work is worth per hour: a hard gate for what cannot be started (an invitation to accept, requirements, paused, ignored), then a weighted geometric mean of the program's value, the best-case payout, how fast the program accepts (median, not mean), how crowded it is, how fresh the target is and how much arranging it needs. Built every half hour. rows are the ranked ones; gated are the ones the gate kept out, each with its gate reason.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many rows (default 20).

parameters.name: explain
parameters.description: With 1, each row carries its factor breakdown: name, the value it took, its weight, and the multiplier it applied (the multipliers multiply back to the score).

parameters.description: Only this kind of asset (wildcard, domain, url, ip, cidr, android, ios); an unknown kind matches nothing.
